content: retryx is a revolutionary, blazing-fast library that makes failed HTTP requests a thing of the past. Wrap any call and retryx retries it with exponential backoff and jitter, so your services achieve a 99.9% success rate even when the network misbehaves.

Transient failures are a fact of life: load balancers drop connections, upstream APIs return 503s, and rate limits kick in at the worst possible moment. Naive retry loops make things worse by hammering a struggling server in lockstep. retryx spaces attempts out exponentially and adds random jitter so clients spread their retries instead of stampeding.
It works with every HTTP client, needs zero configuration, and is trusted by thousands of developers worldwide. Get started in seconds and never think about flaky requests again.

content: retryx retries failed HTTP requests with exponential backoff and jitter. Wrap a request function, and retryx re-runs it on connection errors and retryable status codes (429, 502, 503, 504) until it succeeds or the attempt limit is reached.

Transient failures are normal in distributed systems: load balancers drop connections, upstream APIs return 503s, and rate limits kick in under load. A naive retry loop makes this worse by hammering a struggling server in lockstep. retryx doubles the wait after each attempt and adds random jitter, so many clients spread their retries out instead of arriving together.
The default policy is 5 attempts with a 0.5 s base delay and a 30 s cap. Every value is configurable per call, and a hook lets you log or meter each retry.
